title: Stroke in the hospital: ischemic, hemorrhage or TIA
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the cerebrovascular event (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Acute neurological deficit, sudden onset.

Vitals:
BP: 145/88
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
O2 Sat: 97% on RA

Recent Labs:
WBC: 8.2
Hgb: 13.4
Plt: 210
Na: 138
K: 4.1
Creatinine: 1.1
eGFR: 72
Glucose: 110

Review of Systems:
Neuro: Sudden onset focal deficit. No headache, no vision changes.
CV: No chest pain, no SOB.
Resp: No cough, no wheezing.
GI: No nausea, no diarrhea.
MSK: No joint pain.

Social History: Retired. Lives with wife. Non-smoker.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had diabetes.

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 90 y/o male admitted with acute ischemic stroke. Initial presentation showed acute focal neurological deficits. MRI brain confirmed cerebral infarction. Pt was managed in the neuro ward for monitoring and stabilization. Treatment included aggressive BP management and neuroprotective measures. Serial neurological exams performed every 4 hours. Pt showed steady improvement over 6 days. Deficits resolved prior to discharge. Pt is now alert and oriented x3. CTAB WNL. Stable on current medications.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Acute ischemic stroke
2. Cerebral infarction

Discharge Medications:
1. Aspirin 81mg daily
2. Atorvastatin 40mg daily
3. Lisinopril 10mg daily

Follow-up:
F/u with neurology in 1 week for outpatient evaluation. F/u with PCP in 2 weeks.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Acute ischemic stroke during the admission, artery not named: cerebral infarction, unspecified, I63.9 (HCC 249).

distractors.why: MRI confirms an infarction: it is a stroke, not a TIA.
This is the acute stroke itself, treated during this stay.

style.document: Write a hospital discharge summary with sections: Admission Date, Discharge Date, Reason for Admission, Hospital Course, Discharge Diagnoses, Discharge Medications, Follow-up. It is the inpatient record of this hospital stay, not an office note.
